name: Vitamin B complex
searchTerms: thiamine riboflavin pyridoxine calcium pantothenate niacinamide

formulations.label: Tablets
formulations.strengths: Clinic product: thiamine 2 mg + riboflavin 2 mg + pyridoxine 2 mg + calcium pantothenate 3 mg + niacinamide (nicotinamide) 20 mg per tablet. UK SmPC used: thiamine hydrochloride 5 mg, riboflavin 2 mg, nicotinamide 20 mg, pyridoxine hydrochloride 2 mg per tablet.
formulations.note: No UK SmPC with the clinic's five-vitamin make-up was found. The UK product used (vitamin B compound strong tablets) shares four actives (thiamine, riboflavin, pyridoxine, nicotinamide) but has more thiamine (5 mg vs 2 mg) and contains NO calcium pantothenate. Only statements about the four shared vitamins are shown; calcium pantothenate is not covered by any UK source here. The UK tablet's dose and excipients do not apply to the clinic tablet: use the clinic label for the dose.

src.q: Each coated tablet contains Thiamine HCI 5 mg, Riboflavin 2 mg, Nicotinamide 20 mg and Pyridoxine HC1 2 mg

bnf.note: BNF/BNFC is only available in the UK; not accessed.

items.t: Mild chronic vitamin deficiency; clinical and sub-clinical vitamin B deficiency (e.g. glossitis, stomatitis, cheilosis, beriberi heart signs, pellagra skin signs, corneal vascularisation, polyneuritis).

src.q: For the treatment of mild chronic vitamin deficiency.
For the treatment of clinical and sub-clinical vitamin B deficiency states

restrictions.note: No prescribing restrictions in the UK vitamin B compound strong tablet SmPC (MHRA Products, PL 20416/0410).

items.tag: UK vitamin B compound strong tablet only
items.t: UK vitamin B compound strong tablet: adults and elderly 1-2 tablets three times daily. The clinic tablet has a different make-up: use the clinic label for its dose.

src.q: Adults, elderly and children over 3 years: 1 - 2 tablets three times daily.

items.t: UK vitamin B compound strong tablet: children over 3 years 1-2 tablets three times daily; should not be used in children under 3 years. The clinic tablet has a different make-up: use the clinic label for its dose.

src.q: Adults, elderly and children over 3 years: 1 - 2 tablets three times daily.
Should not be used in children under 3 years.

items.tag: UK vitamin B compound strong tablet only

items.t: Hypersensitivity to thiamine, riboflavin, pyridoxine or nicotinamide.

src.q: Hypersensitivity, to thiamine hydrochloride, riboflavin, pyridoxine hydrochloride and nicotinamide.

cautions.note: The UK vitamin B compound strong SmPC 4.4 lists only lactose-related excipient warnings, which do not apply to the clinic tablet (its excipients are not known). No other warnings.

items.t: Pyridoxine may reduce the effect of plain levodopa: patients with Parkinson's disease on plain levodopa should not take vitamin B6 in doses well above daily needs. Does not apply when levodopa is given with a decarboxylase inhibitor.

src.q: patients with Parkinson's disease who are receiving treatment with plain levodopa should not take vitamin B6 in doses which greatly exceed the daily requirement.
This does not apply when levodopa is combined with a peripheral decarboxylase inhibitor.

renal.note: No renal impairment advice in the UK vitamin B compound strong tablet SmPC (MHRA Products, PL 20416/0410).

hepatic.note: No hepatic impairment advice in the UK vitamin B compound strong tablet SmPC (MHRA Products, PL 20416/0410).

items.t: Limited data. Can be used if needed to correct deficiency and benefit outweighs risk; caution when prescribing in pregnancy.

src.q: can be used in pregnant women if use is necessary to correct deficiencies and if benefits overweighs risks.
Caution should be exercised when prescribing to pregnant women.

items.t: Excreted in milk; no harm expected at recommended doses. High-dose pyridoxine may reduce milk production (prolactin): use with caution in nursing mothers.

src.q: No harm to suckling infant is expected if used in recommended doses.
In high doses, pyridoxine may interfere with prolactin release and should only be used with caution in nursing mothers.
Fertility: No relevant data is available.

items.t: Side effects are unlikely; excess vitamin B is excreted.

src.q: Vitamin B Compound Strong tablets are unlikely to cause any side effects, as any excess vitamin B is naturally excreted from the body.

items.t: Severe allergic reactions (rash, hives, itching, breathing difficulty, chest tightness, swelling of mouth, face, lips or tongue) or numbness/tingling of the skin: seek medical attention right away.

src.q: Seek medical attention right away if any of these SEVERE side effects like severe allergic reactions
numbness or tingling of the skin occur

monitoring.note: No monitoring requirements in the UK vitamin B compound strong tablet SmPC (MHRA Products, PL 20416/0410).
